The user-visible symptom was: every typed\n  // character appeared twice in the terminal, and every line of command\n  // output (e.g. `cargo run`'s \"Hello from rust-web-box!\") rendered\n  // duplicated. The root cause lived in the webvm-host extension: each\n  // call to `makePseudoterminal().open()` did\n  //   `stdoutDispose = bus.on('proc.stdout', …)`\n  // without disposing the previous subscriber. VS Code Web calls open()\n  // more than once per pty (panel reattach, terminal restore), so each\n  // reattach added a fresh listener, and the writeEmitter that fanned\n  // those subscribers into xterm received N copies of every byte.\n  //\n  // We can't reach VS Code's xterm DOM from this harness (the workbench\n  // panel only mounts after a user gesture, and the e2e harness sets\n  // `__RUST_WEB_BOX_SKIP_BASH = true` to avoid the CheerpX 1.3.x 'a1'\n  // OverlayDevice wedge), so we validate the runtime invariants the\n  // extension's fix relies on, exercised against the real page-side bus:\n  //\n  //   1. The page's busServer emits each `proc.stdout` chunk exactly once\n  //      per BroadcastChannel subscriber. (If this regressed, every\n  //      consumer — extension, debugger, future tooling — would see\n  //      doubles regardless of how disciplined they were about\n  //      subscriber lifecycle.)\n  //\n  //   2. The unsubscribe function returned by the page's bus dispatcher\n  //      actually detaches the listener. The extension's fix\n  //      (detachBusListeners() before re-binding) only works if calling\n  //      that disposer stops further deliveries — so this is the runtime\n  //      precondition for the fix.\n  //\n  // The narrow source-shape regression (every `bus.on('proc.stdout', …)`\n  // site in extension.js is preceded by a paired `detachBusListeners()`\n  // call) is asserted separately in\n  // `web/tests/extension-pty-listeners.test.mjs`.\n  const commander = await tryLoadBrowserCommander();\n  if (bailIfMissingPrereqs(t, { commander })) return;\n\n  const server = await startDevServer({ basePrefix: BASE_PREFIX });\n  t.after(() => server.stop());\n\n  await withWorkbench(server.url, async ({ page, errors, diagnostics }) => {\n    const vmPhase = await waitForLinux(page, { diagnostics: { ...diagnostics, errors } });\n    assert.equal(vmPhase, 'ready');\n\n    const result = await page.evaluate(async () => {\n      const busServer = globalThis.__rustWebBox?.busServer;\n      if (!busServer || typeof busServer.emit !== 'function') {\n        throw new Error('page-side busServer not exposed on __rustWebBox');\n      }\n\n      // Sentinel markers that cannot legitimately appear in the stream\n      // unless we put them there.\n      const MARKER_A = 'rwb_dup_check_a_' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10);\n      const MARKER_B = 'rwb_dup_check_b_' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10);\n\n      // Spin up an *independent* BroadcastChannel subscriber — the same\n      // way the webvm-host extension would in its host worker. The bus\n      // server lives in the page; this listener attaches from the same\n      // page context, which still exercises the BroadcastChannel\n      // postMessage → message-event delivery path.\n      const channel = new BroadcastChannel('rust-web-box/webvm-bus');\n      const inbox = [];\n      const onMessage = (ev) => {\n        const msg = ev.data;\n        if (msg?.kind === 'event' && msg.topic === 'proc.stdout' && msg.payload?.chunk) {\n          inbox.push(msg.payload.chunk);\n        }\n      };\n      channel.addEventListener('message', onMessage);\n\n      // Wait one microtask + one macrotask flush so the listener is wired\n      // before we emit. BroadcastChannel postMessage is synchronous-ish\n      // but message dispatch is on the next task; emitting too early\n      // would mask the regression by losing chunks unrelated to the bug.\n      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0));\n\n      // Invariant 1: page-side emit is single-delivery. Emit once and\n      // give the message-event a tick to land. The pre-#27 doubled\n      // pipeline would put MARKER_A in the inbox twice; the fixed\n      // pipeline puts it in once.\n      busServer.emit('proc.stdout', { pid: 1, chunk: MARKER_A });\n      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 100));\n\n      const countA = inbox.filter((c) => c === MARKER_A).length;\n\n      // Invariant 2: subscribers detach cleanly. Remove our listener and\n      // emit a *different* marker — it must not arrive. The extension's\n      // fix (detachBusListeners() before re-binding) is built on this\n      // exact precondition. If `removeEventListener` no-ops here, the\n      // detach pattern in extension.js silently leaks listeners again.\n      channel.removeEventListener('message', onMessage);\n      busServer.emit('proc.stdout', { pid: 1, chunk: MARKER_B });\n      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 100));\n\n      const countB = inbox.filter((c) => c === MARKER_B).length;\n\n      channel.close();\n      return {\n        markerA: MARKER_A,\n        markerB: MARKER_B,\n        countA,\n        countB,\n        inboxSize: inbox.length,\n      };\n    });\n\n    assert.equal(\n      result.countA, 1,\n      `marker ${result.markerA} should appear exactly 1x in proc.stdout ` +\n      `(single-delivery invariant), saw ${result.countA}. ` +\n      `> 1 is the regression returning.`,\n    );\n    assert.equal(\n      result.countB, 0,\n      `marker ${result.markerB} should appear 0x after the listener detached ` +\n      `(disposer invariant), saw ${result.countB}. > 0 means the unsubscribe ` +\n      `function returned by the bus did not actually remove the listener — ` +\n      `the extension's detachBusListeners() fix would silently leak.`,\n    );\n  }, { commander });\n});\n",

Both suites\n// need the same primitives:\n//\n//   - launch a Chromium with cross-origin isolation enabled\n//   - navigate to the workbench URL with COOP/COEP headers\n//   - capture console errors so the suite fails on regressions\n//   - wait for `globalThis.__rustWebBox.shim` to come up — that's our\n//     stage-1 boot signal (workspace ready, CheerpX still loading)\n//   - drive `cx.run` directly to verify `tree`, the shell, and the\n//     pre-built `/workspace/target/release/hello` binary all work end\n//     to end on the same warm disk that ships with Pages\n//\n// We use [`browser-commander`](https://github.com/link-foundation/browser-commander)\n// for browser launch and navigation (issue #15 mandates it) and fall\n// through to `commander.page.evaluate` for the in-page work — the\n// library's documented escape hatch (see issues #35-#38 upstream).\n// Anything we discover that the library should wrap natively is filed\n// under `docs/case-studies/issue-15/upstream-issues/`.\n//\n// The harness is **soft-fails** on missing prerequisites (no Chromium\n// installed, dev-server unable to bind, network blocked) so contributors\n// without the full test toolchain still get a green `node --test`. CI\n// turns those soft skips into hard failures via `RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E=1`.\n\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { existsSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport http from 'node:http';\nimport path from 'node:path';\nimport { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';\n\nconst __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));\nconst WEB_ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..');\nconst REPO_ROOT = path.resolve(WEB_ROOT, '..');\n\n/** Default boot timeout: tweak with RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E_BOOT_MS. */\nexport const DEFAULT_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS = Number.parseInt(\n  process.env.RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E_BOOT_MS || '120000',\n  10,\n);\n\n/** True when `RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E=1` — fail hard instead of skipping. */\nexport const E2E_REQUIRED = process.env.RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E === '1';\n\n/**\n * Returns true when the chunked rust-alpine warm disk is staged under\n * `web/disk/`. That fallback works *at runtime* but doesn't carry `cargo` or\n * `tree`, so the `tree --version` / `cargo run` assertions in our local\n * e2e suite cannot succeed against it.\n */\nexport function isWarmDiskStaged() {\n  const meta = path.join(WEB_ROOT, 'disk', 'rust-alpine.ext2.meta');\n  const firstChunk = path.join(WEB_ROOT, 'disk', 'rust-alpine.ext2.c000000.txt');\n  return existsSync(meta) && existsSync(firstChunk);\n}\n\n/**\n * Try to import `browser-commander`.       resolve();\n      }\n    };\n    const onErr = (chunk) => {\n      output += chunk.toString('utf8');\n    };\n    child.stdout.on('data', onData);\n    child.stderr.on('data', onErr);\n };\n}\n\n/**\n * Capture in-page state for failure diagnostics. The fields we surface are exactly the\n * things we wished we had the first time CheerpX cold-boot stalled in\n * CI: the last-observed `vmPhase`, the booleans for vm/workspace/shim,\n * the disk URL the bridge resolved to, and a bus-level boot history if\n * the page is wired to record it (we add the recorder below).\n */\nasync function captureWorkbenchSnapshot(page) {\n  try {\n    return await page.evaluate(() => {\n      const safe = (v) => {\n        try { return typeof v === 'string' || typeof v === 'number' || typeof v === 'boolean' ? v : Boolean(v); }\n        catch { return null; }\n      };\n      const rwb = globalThis.__rustWebBox || {};\n      return {\n        vmPhase: safe(rwb.vmPhase),\n        hasVm: Boolean(rwb.vm),\n        hasShim: Boolean(rwb.shim),\n        hasWorkspace: Boolean(rwb.workspace),\n        hasBusServer: Boolean(rwb.busServer),\n        diskUrl: safe(rwb.vm && rwb.vm.diskUrl),\n        diskKind: safe(rwb.vm && rwb.vm.diskKind),\n        bootHistory: Array.isArray(globalThis.__rustWebBoxBootHistory)\n          ? globalThis.__rustWebBoxBootHistory.slice(-50)\n          : null,\n        documentTitle: typeof document !== 'undefined' ? document.title : null,\n        readyState: typeof document !== 'undefined' ? document.readyState : null,\n      };\n    });\n  } catch (err) {\n    return { captureError: err?.message ?? String(err) };\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Format the structured timeout context as multi-line text we can attach\n * to a thrown error, so a single-line `Timeout 180000ms exceeded` in a\n * CI log expands into actionable evidence.\n */\nfunction formatTimeoutContext({ stage, snapshot, consoleHistory, errors, failedRequests }) {\n  const lines = [];\n  lines.push(`workbench timeout at stage: ${stage}`);\n  lines.push('--- in-page snapshot ---');\n  lines.push(JSON.stringify(snapshot, null, 2));\n  if (consoleHistory?.length) {\n    lines.push('--- last console messages ---');\n    for (const msg of consoleHistory.slice(-30)) lines.push(msg);\n  }\n  if (errors?.length) {\n    lines.push('--- captured console.error / pageerror ---');\n    for (const e of errors.slice(-20)) lines.push(e);\n  }\n  if (failedRequests?.length) {\n    lines.push('--- failed network requests ---');\n    for (const r of failedRequests.slice(-20)) lines.push(r);\n  }\n  return lines.join('\\n');\n}\n\n/**\n * Drive a single browser session against `url`. On a\n * stage-1 timeout we attach a snapshot + console + network log to the\n * thrown error so CI logs surface the *cause* of the stall rather than\n * just `Timeout Xms exceeded`.\n */\nexport async function withWorkbench(url, body, {\n  commander: commanderMod,\n  bootTimeoutMs = DEFAULT_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS,\n  headless = process.env.RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E_HEADED === '1' ? false : true,\n  // By default we skip the workspace prime AND the interactive bash loop\n  // (see the addInitScript note below). The UI-driven e2e suite needs the\n  // *real* terminal, so it opts back in with `skipPrime: false` +\n  // `skipBash: false`. That is only safe against a disk image whose seed\n  // inodes already exist (a freshly built rust-alpine.ext2), because the\n  // prime then only ever overwrites existing inodes — never allocates the\n  // fresh ones that trip the CheerpX 1.3.x OverlayDevice 'a1' wedge.\n  skipPrime = true,\n  skipBash = true,\n} = {}) {\n  const { launchBrowser, makeBrowserCommander } = commanderMod;\n  // CI builds and most container/sandbox dev environments cannot use\n  // Chromium's seccomp/userns sandbox. We turn it off either when CI=1\n  // or when the user explicitly opts in via RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E_NO_SANDBOX.\n  // Local desktop runs leave the sandbox on for safety.\n  const noSandbox = process.env.CI || process.env.RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E_NO_SANDBOX === '1';\n  const args = noSandbox ? ['--no-sandbox', '--disable-setuid-sandbox'] : [];\n\n  const { browser, page } = await launchBrowser({ engine: 'playwright', headless, args });\n  const commander = makeBrowserCommander({ page, verbose: false });\n\n  const errors = [];\n  const consoleHistory = [];\n  const failedRequests = [];\n  page.on('console', (msg) => {\n    const line = `[${msg.type()}] ${msg.text()}`;\n    consoleHistory.push(line);\n    if (msg.type() === 'error') {\n      // CheerpX writes some \"expected\" warnings to console.error during\n      // boot (CSP for service workers, missing source maps, etc.). We\n      // record everything but the assertion layer filters it.\n      errors.push(msg.text());\n    }\n  });\n  page.on('pageerror', (err) => {\n    errors.push(`pageerror: ${err.message}`);\n    consoleHistory.push(`[pageerror] ${err.message}`);\n  });\n  page.on('requestfailed', (req) => {\n    try {\n      failedRequests.push(`${req.method?.() ?? 'GET'} ${req.url?.() ?? '?'}: ${req.failure?.()?.errorText ?? 'failed'}`);\n    } catch {}\n  });\n  page.on('response', (res) => {\n    try {\n      const status = res.status?.();\n      if (typeof status === 'number' && status >= 400) {\n        failedRequests.push(`HTTP ${status} ${res.url?.()}`);\n      }\n    } catch {}\n  });\n\n  // Inject a recorder for every `vm.boot` payload published on the\n  // workspace's BroadcastChannel. We hook `postMessage` (not\n  // `addEventListener`) because BroadcastChannel does NOT echo messages\n  // back to the sender — only sibling instances receive them, and the\n  // page only opens one channel during boot. `addInitScript` runs before\n  // any page script so we don't miss the early `loading-cheerpx` /\n  // `booting-linux` transitions.\n  //\n  // We don't filter by channel name. The bus uses `'rust-web-box/webvm-bus'`\n  // (CHANNEL_NAME in web/glue/webvm-bus.js), and a stricter `===` check\n  // here previously dropped every event — that's why the in-page snapshot\n  // surfaced `bootHistory: []` even on runs that DID emit phases. Letting\n  // any `vm.boot` event through is fine: the topic + kind discriminator is\n  // unique enough.\n  await page.addInitScript(() => {\n    globalThis.__rustWebBoxBootHistory = [];\n    const origBC = globalThis.BroadcastChannel;\n    if (typeof origBC === 'function') {\n      const origPost = origBC.prototype.postMessage;\n      origBC.prototype.postMessage = function (data) {\n        try {\n          if (data && data.kind === 'event' && data.topic === 'vm.boot') {\n            globalThis.__rustWebBoxBootHistory.push(\n              `${Date.now()} ${this.name || '?'} ${data.payload && data.payload.phase}`,\n            );\n          }\n        } catch {}\n        return origPost.call(this, data);\n      };\n    }\n    // CheerpX 1.3.x has a flaky OverlayDevice bug: writing a brand-new\n    // inode under /workspace can fire `TypeError: …reading 'a1'`,\n    // `Program exited with code 71`, and wedge the runtime so every\n    // subsequent `cx.run` errors with `function signature mismatch`.\n    // See web/glue/webvm-server.js for full notes. The e2e suite runs\n    // against whichever rust-alpine disk image is currently published\n    // (which already ships the seed paths the prime would touch), so\n    // skipping the prime is the safe choice that keeps boot deterministic.\n    globalThis.__RUST_WEB_BOX_SKIP_PRIME = true;\n    globalThis.__RUST_WEB_BOX_SKIP_BASH = true;\n  });\n\n  try {\n    await commander.goto({ url, waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded', timeout: bootTimeoutMs });\n\n    // Stage 1: wait for the workspace shim to populate\n    // `globalThis.__rustWebBox`. Passing `{ timeout }` as the second arg silently falls\n    // through to the default 30s timeout — which is too short for a\n    // cold CheerpX boot in CI. Always pass `undefined` as `arg`.\n    try {\n      await page.waitForFunction(\n        () => Boolean(globalThis.__rustWebBox && globalThis.__rustWebBox.shim),\n        undefined,\n        { timeout: bootTimeoutMs },\n      );\n    } catch (err) {\n      const snapshot = await captureWorkbenchSnapshot(page);\n      const detail = formatTimeoutContext({\n        stage: 'stage-1 (workspace shim)',\n        snapshot,\n        consoleHistory,\n        errors,\n        failedRequests,\n      });\n      err.message = `${err.message}\\n${detail}`;\n      throw err;\n    }\n\n    return await body({ commander, page, errors, diagnostics: { consoleHistory, failedRequests } });\n  } finally {\n    try { await commander.destroy(); } catch {}\n    try { await browser.close(); } catch {}\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Wait until CheerpX has booted Linux (stage 2). Tests should forward the `diagnostics`\n * argument they receive from the body callback so the failure surface is\n * uniform across both stages.\n */\nexport async function waitForLinux(page, { timeoutMs = DEFAULT_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS, diagnostics } = {}) {\n  // See note in `withWorkbench` — `waitForFunction` takes (fn, arg,\n  // options). 'TERM=xterm-256color',\n          'CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0',\n        ],\n        cwd: '/workspace',\n        uid: 0, gid: 0,\n      }),\n      new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(() => resolve(TIMEOUT), We hook `postMessage` (not\n  // `addEventListener`) because BroadcastChannel does NOT echo messages\n  // back to the sender — only sibling instances receive them, and the\n  // page only opens one channel during boot. `addInitScript` runs before\n  // any page script so we don't miss the early `loading-cheerpx` /\n  // `booting-linux` transitions.\n  //\n  // We don't filter by channel name. The pre-#27 doubled\n491\t      // pipeline would put MARKER_A in the inbox twice; the fixed\n492\t      // pipeline puts it in once.\n493\t      busServer.emit('proc.stdout', { pid: 1, chunk: MARKER_A });\n494\t      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 100));\n495\t\n496\t      const countA = inbox.filter((c) => c === MARKER_A).length;\n497\t\n498\t      // Invariant 2: subscribers detach cleanly. The user-visible symptom was: every typed\n  // character appeared twice in the terminal, and every line of command\n  // output (e.g. `cargo run`'s \"Hello from rust-web-box!\") rendered\n  // duplicated. The root cause lived in the webvm-host extension: each\n  // call to `makePseudoterminal().open()` did\n  //   `stdoutDispose = bus.on('proc.stdout', …)`\n  // without disposing the previous subscriber. VS Code Web calls open()\n  // more than once per pty (panel reattach, terminal restore), so each\n  // reattach added a fresh listener, and the writeEmitter that fanned\n  // those subscribers into xterm received N copies of every byte.\n  //\n  // We can't reach VS Code's xterm DOM from this harness (the workbench\n  // panel only mounts after a user gesture, and the e2e harness sets\n  // `__RUST_WEB_BOX_SKIP_BASH = true` to avoid the CheerpX 1.3.x 'a1'\n  // OverlayDevice wedge), so we validate the runtime invariants the\n  // extension's fix relies on, exercised against the real page-side bus:\n  //\n  //   1. The page's busServer emits each `proc.stdout` chunk exactly once\n  //      per BroadcastChannel subscriber. (If this regressed, every\n  //      consumer — extension, debugger, future tooling — would see\n  //      doubles regardless of how disciplined they were about\n  //      subscriber lifecycle.)\n  //\n  //   2. The unsubscribe function returned by the page's bus dispatcher\n  //      actually detaches the listener. The extension's fix\n  //      (detachBusListeners() before re-binding) only works if calling\n  //      that disposer stops further deliveries — so this is the runtime\n  //      precondition for the fix.\n  //\n  // The narrow source-shape regression (every `bus.on('proc.stdout', …)`\n  // site in extension.js is preceded by a paired `detachBusListeners()`\n  // call) is asserted separately in\n  // `web/tests/extension-pty-listeners.test.mjs`.\n  const commander = await tryLoadBrowserCommander();\n  if (bailIfMissingPrereqs(t, { commander })) return;\n\n  const server = await startDevServer({ basePrefix: BASE_PREFIX });\n  t.after(() => server.stop());\n\n  await withWorkbench(server.url, async ({ page, errors, diagnostics }) => {\n    const vmPhase = await waitForLinux(page, { diagnostics: { ...diagnostics, errors } });\n    assert.equal(vmPhase, 'ready');\n\n    const result = await page.evaluate(async () => {\n      const busServer = globalThis.__rustWebBox?.busServer;\n      if (!busServer || typeof busServer.emit !== 'function') {\n        throw new Error('page-side busServer not exposed on __rustWebBox');\n      }\n\n      // Sentinel markers that cannot legitimately appear in the stream\n      // unless we put them there.\n      const MARKER_A = 'rwb_dup_check_a_' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10);\n      const MARKER_B = 'rwb_dup_check_b_' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10);\n\n      // Spin up an *independent* BroadcastChannel subscriber — the same\n      // way the webvm-host extension would in its host worker. The bus\n      // server lives in the page; this listener attaches from the same\n      // page context, which still exercises the BroadcastChannel\n      // postMessage → message-event delivery path.\n      const channel = new BroadcastChannel('rust-web-box/webvm-bus');\n      const inbox = [];\n      const onMessage = (ev) => {\n        const msg = ev.data;\n        if (msg?.kind === 'event' && msg.topic === 'proc.stdout' && msg.payload?.chunk) {\n          inbox.push(msg.payload.chunk);\n        }\n      };\n      channel.addEventListener('message', onMessage);\n\n      // Wait one microtask + one macrotask flush so the listener is wired\n      // before we emit. BroadcastChannel postMessage is synchronous-ish\n      // but message dispatch is on the next task; emitting too early\n      // would mask the regression by losing chunks unrelated to the bug.\n      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0));\n\n      // Invariant 1: page-side emit is single-delivery. Emit once and\n      // give the message-event a tick to land. The pre-#27 doubled\n      // pipeline would put MARKER_A in the inbox twice; the fixed\n      // pipeline puts it in once.\n      busServer.emit('proc.stdout', { pid: 1, chunk: MARKER_A });\n      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 100));\n\n      const countA = inbox.filter((c) => c === MARKER_A).length;\n\n      // Invariant 2: subscribers detach cleanly. Remove our listener and\n      // emit a *different* marker — it must not arrive. The extension's\n      // fix (detachBusListeners() before re-binding) is built on this\n      // exact precondition. If `removeEventListener` no-ops here, the\n      // detach pattern in extension.js silently leaks listeners again.\n      channel.removeEventListener('message', onMessage);\n      busServer.emit('proc.stdout', { pid: 1, chunk: MARKER_B });\n      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 100));\n\n      const countB = inbox.filter((c) => c === MARKER_B).length;\n\n      channel.close();\n      return {\n        markerA: MARKER_A,\n        markerB: MARKER_B,\n        countA,\n        countB,\n        inboxSize: inbox.length,\n      };\n    });\n\n    assert.equal(\n      result.countA, 1,\n      `marker ${result.markerA} should appear exactly 1x in proc.stdout ` +\n      `(single-delivery invariant), saw ${result.countA}. ` +\n      `> 1 is the regression returning.`,\n    );\n    assert.equal(\n      result.countB, 0,\n      `marker ${result.markerB} should appear 0x after the listener detached ` +\n      `(disposer invariant), saw ${result.countB}. > 0 means the unsubscribe ` +\n      `function returned by the bus did not actually remove the listener — ` +\n      `the extension's detachBusListeners() fix would silently leak.`,\n    );\n  }, { commander });\n});\n",

The function is\n    // called once per chunk of guest stdout/stderr; `vt` is the virtual\n    // terminal index — we only collect vt=1 (the foreground tty).\n    const chunks = [];\n    const decoder = new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: false });\n    const writer = (buf, vt) => {\n      if (vt !== undefined && vt !== 1) return;\n      let view;\n      if (buf instanceof Uint8Array) view = buf;\n      else if (buf instanceof ArrayBuffer) view = new Uint8Array(buf);\n      else if (Array.isArray(buf)) view = new Uint8Array(buf);\n      else return;\n      chunks.push(decoder.decode(view, { stream: true }));\n    };\n    cx.setCustomConsole(writer, 80, 24);\n    // CheerpX 1.3.x has a flaky 'a1' bug where cx.run can hang forever\n    // after a runtime crash (the JS-level promise never settles). guardedCommand = [\n      '__rwb_apply_cargo_profile() {',\n      '  [ -f /root/.cargo/config.toml ] || return 0',\n      \"  grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*debug[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*0[[:space:]]*$' CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0',\n      '  export CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_CODEGEN_UNITS=1',\n      '  export CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_INCREMENTAL=false',\n      '}',\n      '__rwb_apply_cargo_profile',\n      'unset -f __rwb_apply_cargo_profile 2>/dev/null || true',\n      command,\n    ].join('\\n');\n    const winner = await Promise.race([\n      cx.run('/bin/sh', ['-c', guardedCommand], {\n        // Match 'TERM=xterm-256color',\n          'CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0',\n        ],\n        cwd: '/workspace',\n        uid: 0, gid: 0,\n      }),\n      new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(() => resolve(TIMEOUT), output: chunks.join(''), timedOut: false };\n  }, { command, timeoutMs });\n}\n\nexport async function hasLeanCargoDevProfile(page) {\n  const result = await runInVM(\n    page,\n    [\n      \"grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*debug[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*0[[:space:]]*$' /root/.cargo/config.toml\",\n      \"grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*codegen-units[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*1[[:space:]]*$' First cargo run + output,\n//    file change (using VS Code UI - editor), cargo run + verify output\n//    (all using VS Code terminal).\"\n//\n// Unlike `local-pages-e2e.test.mjs` (which drives the VM through `cx.run`\n// and the bus, with the interactive bash *disabled* to dodge the CheerpX\n// 1.3.x OverlayDevice 'a1' wedge), this suite exercises the **actual UI a\n// user touches**:\n//\n//   Step 1 — type `cargo run` into the real integrated terminal (xterm),\n//            press Enter, and verify the seed greeting \"Hello, world!\"\n//            appears in the terminal output.\n//   Step 2 — edit /workspace/src/main.rs in the real Monaco editor\n//            (select-all, replace with a uniquely-marked greeting), and\n//            save with Ctrl+S — the genuine VS Code FileSystemProvider\n//            save path.\n//   Step 3 — type `cargo run` again in the terminal and verify the *new*\n//            unique marker appears AND that cargo printed \"Compiling\".\n//\n// Steps 2+3 together are the anti-fake proof the issue demands: a cached\n// or pre-baked binary cannot print a marker that did not exist until this\n// run, and \"Compiling\" proves CheerpX genuinely re-invoked rustc inside\n// the VM rather than replaying a stale artifact.\n//\n// Why this needs the real shell + prime (skipPrime:false, skipBash:false):\n//   The terminal keystroke path is handleInput -> proc.write ->\n//   `cx.setCustomConsole` reader -> the long-lived `/bin/bash --login`\n//   loop (`runShellLoop` in webvm-server.js). With `__RUST_WEB_BOX_SKIP_BASH`\n//   set (the default for the other suites) that loop never starts, so\n//   keystrokes go nowhere. Both budgets are\n// overridable so a slow CI runner can be given more headroom without an\n// edit.\nconst RUN1_TIMEOUT_MS = Number.parseInt(process.env.RUST_WEB_BOX_UI_RUN1_MS || '180000', 10);\nconst REBUILD_TIMEOUT_MS = Number.parseInt(process.env.RUST_WEB_BOX_UI_REBUILD_MS || '420000', 10);\n// Where to drop human-reviewable evidence (terminal transcript + final\n// screenshot). Returns `true` when\n * the test should bail.\n */\nfunction bailIfMissingPrereqs(t, { commander }) {\n  if (!E2E_REQUIRED && process.env.RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E_NO_SANDBOX !== '1') {\n    t.skip('set RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E=1 to run the UI-driven e2e suite');\n    return true;\n  }\n  if (!commander) {\n    if (E2E_REQUIRED) throw new Error('browser-commander is required when RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E=1');\n    t.skip('browser-commander / playwright not installed; skipping UI e2e');\n    return true;\n  }\n  if (!vendoredCheerpx()) {\n    if (E2E_REQUIRED) {\n      throw new Error('web/cheerpx/cx.esm.js missing — run `node web/build/build-workbench.mjs` first');\n    }\n    t.skip('CheerpX not vendored; run `node web/build/build-workbench.mjs` first');\n    return true;\n  }\n  if (!vendoredVSCodeWeb()) {\n    if (E2E_REQUIRED) {\n      throw new Error('web/vscode-web/out/vs/workbench/workbench.web.main.js missing — run `node web/build/build-workbench.mjs` first');\n    }\n    t.skip('VS Code Web not vendored; run `node web/build/build-workbench.mjs` first');\n    return true;\n  }\n  if (!isWarmDiskStaged()) {\n    // The UI suite types real `cargo run` commands and asserts on the\n    // seed greeting + a fresh rebuild. Bounded so a runaway build log\n * can't exhaust page memory.\n */\nasync function installStdoutCollector(page) {\n  await page.evaluate(() => {\n    if (globalThis.__rwbUiStdoutChannel) return;\n    globalThis.__rwbUiStdout = '';\n    const ch = new BroadcastChannel('rust-web-box/webvm-bus');\n    ch.addEventListener('message', (ev) => {\n      const m = ev.data;\n      if (m && m.kind === 'event' && m.topic === 'proc.stdout' && m.payload && typeof m.payload.chunk === 'string') {\n        globalThis.__rwbUiStdout += m.payload.chunk;\n        if (globalThis.__rwbUiStdout.length > 2_000_000) {\n          globalThis.__rwbUiStdout = globalThis.__rwbUiStdout.slice(-1_500_000);\n        }\n      }\n    });\n    globalThis.__rwbUiStdoutChannel = ch;\n  });\n}\n\nasync function readStdout(page) {\n  return await page.evaluate(() => globalThis.__rwbUiStdout || '');\n}\n\n/**\n * Extract the first `println!(\"…\")` literal from Rust source and decode the\n * handful of escapes a hello-world greeting can contain. Mirrors\n * `firstSourceGreeting` in the harness so Step 1 asserts on whatever the\n * staged disk actually seeds — robust across the version-skew window where a\n * PR build may stage a previously published disk image. Returns null when no\n * println is found.\n */\nfunction extractGreeting(source) {\n  const m = String(source).match(/println!\\(\\s*\"((?:[^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*)\"/);\n  if (!m) return null;\n  return m[1]\n    .replace(/\\\\n/g, '\\n')\n    .replace(/\\\\t/g, '\\t')\n    .replace(/\\\\\"/g, '\"')\n    .replace(/\\\\\\\\/g, '\\\\');\n}\n\n// Strip CSI/SGR escapes (cargo colourises \"Compiling\"/\"Finished\") so plain\n// substring assertions are robust. The server already filters the\n// workspace-sync and cargo-bench OSC frames before they reach proc.stdout.\nfunction stripAnsi(s) {\n  return String(s)\n    .replace(/\\x1b\\][^\\x07\\x1b]*(?:\\x07|\\x1b\\\\)/g, '')\n    .replace(/\\x1b[\\[\\]][0-9;?]*[A-Za-z]/g, '')\n    .replace(/\\x1b[=>]/g, '');\n}\n\n/**\n * Poll the captured terminal output until the slice after `sinceIndex`\n * contains every needle in `contains`. Throws a diagnostic error (with the\n * tail of what we did see) on timeout so a stuck build or a corrupted edit\n * surfaces its cause, not just \"timed out\".\n */\nasync function waitForTerminalOutput(page, { contains, sinceIndex = 0, timeoutMs, label, intervalMs = 2000 }) {\n  const needles = Array.isArray(contains) ? contains : [contains];\n  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;\n  let lastDelta = '';\n  for (;;) {\n    const full = await readStdout(page);\n    const delta = stripAnsi(full.slice(sinceIndex));\n    lastDelta = delta;\n    if (needles.every((n) => delta.includes(n))) return { full, deltaStart: sinceIndex };\n    if (Date.now() >= deadline) {\n      const tail = lastDelta.slice(-3000);\n      throw new Error(\n        `[ui-e2e] timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms waiting for ${label} ` +\n        `(needed all of ${JSON.stringify(needles)}).\\n` +\n        `--- terminal output tail (ANSI-stripped) ---\\n${tail}`,\n      );\n    }\n    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, intervalMs));\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Focus the integrated terminal's xterm surface so subsequent\n * page.keyboard input is delivered as real keystrokes\n * (handleInput -> proc.write). Tries a few selectors across VS Code\n * versions.\n */\nasync function focusTerminal(page) {\n  const selectors = [\n    '.terminal-wrapper.active .xterm-screen',\n    '.terminal-outer-container .xterm-screen',\n    '.xterm-screen',\n    '.terminal .xterm',\n    '.xterm',\n  ];\n  for (const sel of selectors) {\n    const el = await page.$(sel);\n    if (el) {\n      await el.click();\n      return sel;\n    }\n  }\n  throw new Error('[ui-e2e] could not find the integrated terminal (.xterm) to focus');\n}\n\n/**\n * Focus the Monaco editor showing main.rs. Retries because\n * the pty's open() (which calls proc.spawn) fires shortly after the\n * extension reveals the terminal, and keystrokes typed before that are\n * dropped.\n */\nasync function intervalMs: 500,\n      });\n      return;\n    } catch {\n      // pty not live yet — reveal/focus and retry.\n      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1500));\n    }\n  }\n  const tail = First cargo run + output,\n//    file change (using VS Code UI - editor), cargo run + verify output\n//    (all using VS Code terminal).\"\n//\n// Unlike `local-pages-e2e.test.mjs` (which drives the VM through `cx.run`\n// and the bus, with the interactive bash *disabled* to dodge the CheerpX\n// 1.3.x OverlayDevice 'a1' wedge), this suite exercises the **actual UI a\n// user touches**:\n//\n//   Step 1 — type `cargo run` into the real integrated terminal (xterm),\n//            press Enter, and verify the seed greeting \"Hello, world!\"\n//            appears in the terminal output.\n//   Step 2 — edit /workspace/src/main.rs in the real Monaco editor\n//            (select-all, replace with a uniquely-marked greeting), and\n//            save with Ctrl+S — the genuine VS Code FileSystemProvider\n//            save path.\n//   Step 3 — type `cargo run` again in the terminal and verify the *new*\n//            unique marker appears AND that cargo printed \"Compiling\".\n//\n// Steps 2+3 together are the anti-fake proof the issue demands: a cached\n// or pre-baked binary cannot print a marker that did not exist until this\n// run, and \"Compiling\" proves CheerpX genuinely re-invoked rustc inside\n// the VM rather than replaying a stale artifact.\n//\n// Why this needs the real shell + prime (skipPrime:false, skipBash:false):\n//   The terminal keystroke path is handleInput -> proc.write ->\n//   `cx.setCustomConsole` reader -> the long-lived `/bin/bash --login`\n//   loop (`runShellLoop` in webvm-server.js). Booting the real bash is only safe on a disk\n//   whose seed inodes all already exist (the warm rust-alpine image or a\n//   freshly built one), because the prime then only overwrites existing\n//   inodes and never allocates the fresh ones that trip the 'a1' wedge.\n//\n// This is a *slow* suite by design (a real debug rebuild inside CheerpX\n// is minutes long — that is the very thing issue #41 measures), so it is\n// dispatched on demand via `.github/workflows/ui-e2e.yml`, never on push.\n// Locally it soft-skips unless RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E=1 (and a browser + warm\n// disk are present), exactly like the other e2e suites.\n//\n// To run with a visible browser locally (needs a staged warm disk):\n//   RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E=1 RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E_HEADED=1 \\\n//     node --test web/tests/e2e/ui-driven-e2e.test.mjs\n\nimport { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { existsSync, mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport path from 'node:path';\n\nimport {\n  DEFAULT_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS,\n  E2E_REQUIRED,\n  WEB_ROOT,\n  isWarmDiskStaged,\n  startDevServer,\n  tryLoadBrowserCommander,\n  waitForLinux,\n  withWorkbench,\n} from '../helpers/cheerpx-page-harness.mjs';\n\nconst BASE_PREFIX = '/rust-web-box';\n\n// Step 1 (`cargo run` on the pre-baked debug binary) is fast; Step 3 is a\n// real rebuild and can take minutes inside CheerpX. Both budgets are\n// overridable so a slow CI runner can be given more headroom without an\n// edit.\nconst RUN1_TIMEOUT_MS = Number.parseInt(process.env.RUST_WEB_BOX_UI_RUN1_MS || '180000', 10);\nconst REBUILD_TIMEOUT_MS = Number.parseInt(process.env.RUST_WEB_BOX_UI_REBUILD_MS || '420000', 10);\n// Where to drop human-reviewable evidence (terminal transcript + final\n// screenshot). The workflow sets this and uploads the directory.\nconst ARTIFACT_DIR = process.env.RUST_WEB_BOX_UI_ARTIFACT_DIR || '';\n\nfunction vendoredCheerpx() {\n  return existsSync(path.join(WEB_ROOT, 'cheerpx', 'cx.esm.js'));\n}\n\nfunction vendoredVSCodeWeb() {\n  return existsSync(path.join(WEB_ROOT, 'vscode-web', 'out', 'vs', 'workbench', 'workbench.web.main.js'));\n}\n\n/**\n * Soft-skip (or hard-fail under RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E=1) for every prerequisite\n * this UI suite needs but cannot bootstrap on its own. Returns `true` when\n * the test should bail.\n */\nfunction bailIfMissingPrereqs(t, { commander }) {\n  if (!E2E_REQUIRED && process.env.RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E_NO_SANDBOX !== '1') {\n    t.skip('set RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E=1 to run the UI-driven e2e suite');\n    return true;\n  }\n  if (!commander) {\n    if (E2E_REQUIRED) throw new Error('browser-commander is required when RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E=1');\n    t.skip('browser-commander / playwright not installed; skipping UI e2e');\n    return true;\n  }\n  if (!vendoredCheerpx()) {\n    if (E2E_REQUIRED) {\n      throw new Error('web/cheerpx/cx.esm.js missing — run `node web/build/build-workbench.mjs` first');\n    }\n    t.skip('CheerpX not vendored; run `node web/build/build-workbench.mjs` first');\n    return true;\n  }\n  if (!vendoredVSCodeWeb()) {\n    if (E2E_REQUIRED) {\n      throw new Error('web/vscode-web/out/vs/workbench/workbench.web.main.js missing — run `node web/build/build-workbench.mjs` first');\n    }\n    t.skip('VS Code Web not vendored; run `node web/build/build-workbench.mjs` first');\n    return true;\n  }\n  if (!isWarmDiskStaged()) {\n    // The UI suite types real `cargo run` commands and asserts on the\n    // seed greeting + a fresh rebuild. Both need the rust-alpine warm\n    // disk (it bakes cargo, the toolchain, and the pre-built binary); the\n    // public Debian fallback can't satisfy them. Booting the real\n    // interactive bash is also only 'a1'-wedge-safe on this disk.\n    if (E2E_REQUIRED) {\n      throw new Error(\n        'warm rust-alpine disk is not staged under web/disk/ — run ' +\n        '`WARM_DISK_SOURCE_URL=https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-web-box/releases/download/disk-latest/rust-alpine.ext2 ' +\n        'node web/build/stage-pages-disk.mjs` first',\n      );\n    }\n    t.skip('warm rust-alpine disk not staged; run web/build/stage-pages-disk.mjs to enable UI e2e');\n    return true;\n  }\n  return false;\n}\n\n/**\n * One bus round-trip (same channel + envelope VS Code's extension uses).\n * Used here only for read-only verification (`fs.readFile`) so it never\n * touches the interactive console the real bash owns.\n */\nasync function requestWorkbenchBus(page, method, params, { timeoutMs = 60_000 } = {}) {\n  return await page.evaluate(async ({ method, params, timeoutMs }) => {\n    const channel = new BroadcastChannel('rust-web-box/webvm-bus');\n    const id = Math.floor(Math.random() * 1_000_000_000);\n    try {\n      return await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n        const timer = setTimeout(\n          () => reject(new Error(`bus request timed out: ${method}`)),\n          timeoutMs,\n        );\n        channel.addEventListener('message', (ev) => {\n          const msg = ev.data;\n          if (!msg || msg.kind !== 'response' || msg.id !== id) return;\n          clearTimeout(timer);\n          if (msg.error) reject(new Error(msg.error.message));\n          else resolve(msg.result);\n        });\n        channel.postMessage({ id, kind: 'request', method, params });\n      });\n    } finally {\n      channel.close();\n    }\n  }, { method, params, timeoutMs });\n}\n\n/**\n * Install a sibling BroadcastChannel that records every `proc.stdout`\n * chunk the page-side bus server emits. BroadcastChannel does not deliver\n * to the exact instance that posted, but a *separate* instance in the same\n * page does receive them — so this faithfully mirrors what the terminal\n * sees, independent of VS Code's xterm DOM. Bounded so a runaway build log\n * can't exhaust page memory.\n */\nasync function installStdoutCollector(page) {\n  await page.evaluate(() => {\n    if (globalThis.__rwbUiStdoutChannel) return;\n    globalThis.__rwbUiStdout = '';\n    const ch = new BroadcastChannel('rust-web-box/webvm-bus');\n    ch.addEventListener('message', (ev) => {\n      const m = ev.data;\n      if (m && m.kind === 'event' && m.topic === 'proc.stdout' && m.payload && typeof m.payload.chunk === 'string') {\n        globalThis.__rwbUiStdout += m.payload.chunk;\n        if (globalThis.__rwbUiStdout.length > 2_000_000) {\n          globalThis.__rwbUiStdout = globalThis.__rwbUiStdout.slice(-1_500_000);\n        }\n      }\n    });\n    globalThis.__rwbUiStdoutChannel = ch;\n  });\n}\n\nasync function readStdout(page) {\n  return await page.evaluate(() => globalThis.__rwbUiStdout || '');\n}\n\n/**\n * Extract the first `println!(\"…\")` literal from Rust source and decode the\n * handful of escapes a hello-world greeting can contain. Mirrors\n * `firstSourceGreeting` in the harness so Step 1 asserts on whatever the\n * staged disk actually seeds — robust across the version-skew window where a\n * PR build may stage a previously published disk image. Returns null when no\n * println is found.\n */\nfunction extractGreeting(source) {\n  const m = String(source).match(/println!\\(\\s*\"((?:[^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*)\"/);\n  if (!m) return null;\n  return m[1]\n    .replace(/\\\\n/g, '\\n')\n    .replace(/\\\\t/g, '\\t')\n    .replace(/\\\\\"/g, '\"')\n    .replace(/\\\\\\\\/g, '\\\\');\n}\n\n// Strip CSI/SGR escapes (cargo colourises \"Compiling\"/\"Finished\") so plain\n// substring assertions are robust. The server already filters the\n// workspace-sync and cargo-bench OSC frames before they reach proc.stdout.\nfunction stripAnsi(s) {\n  return String(s)\n    .replace(/\\x1b\\][^\\x07\\x1b]*(?:\\x07|\\x1b\\\\)/g, '')\n    .replace(/\\x1b[\\[\\]][0-9;?]*[A-Za-z]/g, '')\n    .replace(/\\x1b[=>]/g, '');\n}\n\n/**\n * Poll the captured terminal output until the slice after `sinceIndex`\n * contains every needle in `contains`. Throws a diagnostic error (with the\n * tail of what we did see) on timeout so a stuck build or a corrupted edit\n * surfaces its cause, not just \"timed out\".\n */\nasync function waitForTerminalOutput(page, { contains, sinceIndex = 0, timeoutMs, label, intervalMs = 2000 }) {\n  const needles = Array.isArray(contains) ? contains : [contains];\n  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;\n  let lastDelta = '';\n  for (;;) {\n    const full = await readStdout(page);\n    const delta = stripAnsi(full.slice(sinceIndex));\n    lastDelta = delta;\n    if (needles.every((n) => delta.includes(n))) return { full, deltaStart: sinceIndex };\n    if (Date.now() >= deadline) {\n      const tail = lastDelta.slice(-3000);\n      throw new Error(\n        `[ui-e2e] timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms waiting for ${label} ` +\n        `(needed all of ${JSON.stringify(needles)}).\\n` +\n        `--- terminal output tail (ANSI-stripped) ---\\n${tail}`,\n      );\n    }\n    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, intervalMs));\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Focus the integrated terminal's xterm surface so subsequent\n * page.keyboard input is delivered as real keystrokes\n * (handleInput -> proc.write). Tries a few selectors across VS Code\n * versions.\n */\nasync function focusTerminal(page) {\n  const selectors = [\n    '.terminal-wrapper.active .xterm-screen',\n    '.terminal-outer-container .xterm-screen',\n    '.xterm-screen',\n    '.terminal .xterm',\n    '.xterm',\n  ];\n  for (const sel of selectors) {\n    const el = await page.$(sel);\n    if (el) {\n      await el.click();\n      return sel;\n    }\n  }\n  throw new Error('[ui-e2e] could not find the integrated terminal (.xterm) to focus');\n}\n\n/**\n * Focus the Monaco editor showing main.rs. Clicks the main.rs tab first\n * (it auto-opens active, but a stray welcome tab could steal focus), then\n * clicks the visible text region so the caret lands in the document.\n */\nasync function focusMainEditor(page) {\n  const tab = await page.$('.tab[aria-label*=\"main.rs\"]');\n  if (tab) {\n    try { await tab.click(); } catch { /* tab may already be active */ }\n  }\n  const selectors = [\n    '.editor-group-container.active .monaco-editor .view-lines',\n    '.editor-instance .monaco-editor .view-lines',\n    '.monaco-editor .view-lines',\n  ];\n  for (const sel of selectors) {\n    const el = await page.$(sel);\n    if (el) {\n      await el.click();\n      return sel;\n    }\n  }\n  throw new Error('[ui-e2e] could not find the main.rs Monaco editor to focus');\n}\n\n/** Type a command into the focused terminal and submit it with Enter. */\nasync function runInTerminal(page, command) {\n  await page.keyboard.type(command, { delay: 8 });\n  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');\n}\n\n/**\n * Handshake: prove the terminal is wired end-to-end (xterm -> proc.write\n * -> bash -> proc.stdout -> our collector) before we depend on it. Retries because\n * the pty's open() (which calls proc.spawn) fires shortly after the\n * extension reveals the terminal, and keystrokes typed before that are\n * dropped.\n */\nasync function intervalMs: 500,\n      });\n      return;\n    } catch {\n      // pty not live yet — reveal/focus and retry.\n      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1500));\n    }\n  }\n  const tail = stripAnsi(await readStdout(page)).slice(-2000);\n  throw new Error(\n    `[ui-e2e] integrated terminal never became interactive ` +\n    `(sentinel ${sentinel} never echoed back).\\n` +\n    `--- terminal output tail ---\\n${tail}`,\n  );\n}\n\nfunction writeArtifact(name, contents) {\n  if (!ARTIFACT_DIR) return;\n  try {\n    mkdirSync(ARTIFACT_DIR, { recursive: true });\n mkdirSync(ARTIFACT_DIR, { recursive: true });\n    await page.screenshot({ path: path.join(ARTIFACT_DIR, name), fullPage: true });\n  } catch (err) {\n    // eslint-disable-next-line no-console\n    console.warn(`[ui-e2e] could not capture screenshot ${name}:`, err?.message ?? err);\n  }\n}\n\ntest(\n  'ui e2e: cargo run → edit main.rs in the editor → cargo run reflects the edit (issue #41)',\n First cargo run + output,\n//    file change (using VS Code UI - editor), cargo run + verify output\n//    (all using VS Code terminal).\"\n//\n// Unlike `local-pages-e2e.test.mjs` (which drives the VM through `cx.run`\n// and the bus, with the interactive bash *disabled* to dodge the CheerpX\n// 1.3.x OverlayDevice 'a1' wedge), this suite exercises the **actual UI a\n// user touches**:\n//\n//   Step 1 — type `cargo run` into the real integrated terminal (xterm),\n//            press Enter, and verify the seed greeting \"Hello, world!\"\n//            appears in the terminal output.\n//   Step 2 — edit /workspace/src/main.rs in the real Monaco editor\n//            (select-all, replace with a uniquely-marked greeting), and\n//            save with Ctrl+S — the genuine VS Code FileSystemProvider\n//            save path.\n//   Step 3 — type `cargo run` again in the terminal and verify the *new*\n//            unique marker appears AND that cargo printed \"Compiling\".\n//\n// Steps 2+3 together are the anti-fake proof the issue demands: a cached\n// or pre-baked binary cannot print a marker that did not exist until this\n// run, and \"Compiling\" proves CheerpX genuinely re-invoked rustc inside\n// the VM rather than replaying a stale artifact.\n//\n// Why this needs the real shell + prime (skipPrime:false, skipBash:false):\n//   The terminal keystroke path is handleInput -> proc.write ->\n//   `cx.setCustomConsole` reader -> the long-lived `/bin/bash --login`\n//   loop (`runShellLoop` in webvm-server.js). With `__RUST_WEB_BOX_SKIP_BASH`\n//   set (the default for the other suites) that loop never starts, so\n//   keystrokes go nowhere. Booting the real bash is only safe on a disk\n//   whose seed inodes all already exist (the warm rust-alpine image or a\n//   freshly built one), because the prime then only overwrites existing\n//   inodes and never allocates the fresh ones that trip the 'a1' wedge.\n//\n// This is a *slow* suite by design (a real debug rebuild inside CheerpX\n// is minutes long — that is the very thing issue #41 measures), so it is\n// dispatched on demand via `.github/workflows/ui-e2e.yml`, never on push.\n// Locally it soft-skips unless RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E=1 (and a browser + warm\n// disk are present), exactly like the other e2e suites.\n//\n// To run with a visible browser locally (needs a staged warm disk):\n//   RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E=1 RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E_HEADED=1 \\\n//     node --test web/tests/e2e/ui-driven-e2e.test.mjs\n\nimport { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { existsSync, mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport path from 'node:path';\n\nimport {\n  DEFAULT_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS,\n  E2E_REQUIRED,\n  WEB_ROOT,\n  isWarmDiskStaged,\n  startDevServer,\n  tryLoadBrowserCommander,\n  waitForLinux,\n  withWorkbench,\n} from '../helpers/cheerpx-page-harness.mjs';\n\nconst BASE_PREFIX = '/rust-web-box';\n\n// Step 1 (`cargo run` on the pre-baked debug binary) is fast; Step 3 is a\n// real rebuild and can take minutes inside CheerpX. Returns `true` when\n * the test should bail.\n */\nfunction bailIfMissingPrereqs(t, { commander }) {\n  if (!E2E_REQUIRED && process.env.RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E_NO_SANDBOX !== '1') {\n    t.skip('set RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E=1 to run the UI-driven e2e suite');\n    return true;\n  }\n  if (!commander) {\n    if (E2E_REQUIRED) throw new Error('browser-commander is required when RUST_WEB_BOX_E2E=1');\n    t.skip('browser-commander / playwright not installed; skipping UI e2e');\n    return true;\n  }\n  if (!vendoredCheerpx()) {\n    if (E2E_REQUIRED) {\n      throw new Error('web/cheerpx/cx.esm.js missing — run `node web/build/build-workbench.mjs` first');\n    }\n    t.skip('CheerpX not vendored; run `node web/build/build-workbench.mjs` first');\n    return true;\n  }\n  if (!vendoredVSCodeWeb()) {\n    if (E2E_REQUIRED) {\n      throw new Error('web/vscode-web/out/vs/workbench/workbench.web.main.js missing — run `node web/build/build-workbench.mjs` first');\n    }\n    t.skip('VS Code Web not vendored; run `node web/build/build-workbench.mjs` first');\n    return true;\n  }\n  if (!isWarmDiskStaged()) {\n    // The UI suite types real `cargo run` commands and asserts on the\n    // seed greeting + a fresh rebuild. Booting the real\n    // interactive bash is also only 'a1'-wedge-safe on this disk.\n    if (E2E_REQUIRED) {\n      throw new Error(\n        'warm rust-alpine disk is not staged under web/disk/ — run ' +\n        '`WARM_DISK_SOURCE_URL=https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-web-box/releases/download/disk-latest/rust-alpine.ext2 ' +\n        'node web/build/stage-pages-disk.mjs` first',\n      );\n    }\n    t.skip('warm rust-alpine disk not staged; run web/build/stage-pages-disk.mjs to enable UI e2e');\n    return true;\n  }\n  return false;\n}\n\n/**\n * One bus round-trip (same channel + envelope VS Code's extension uses).\n * Used here only for read-only verification (`fs.readFile`) so it never\n * touches the interactive console the real bash owns.\n */\nasync function requestWorkbenchBus(page, method, params, { timeoutMs = 60_000 } = {}) {\n  return await page.evaluate(async ({ method, params, timeoutMs }) => {\n    const channel = new BroadcastChannel('rust-web-box/webvm-bus');\n    const id = Math.floor(Math.random() * 1_000_000_000);\n    try {\n      return await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n        const timer = setTimeout(\n          () => reject(new Error(`bus request timed out: ${method}`)),\n          timeoutMs,\n        );\n        channel.addEventListener('message', (ev) => {\n          const msg = ev.data;\n          if (!msg || msg.kind !== 'response' || msg.id !== id) return;\n          clearTimeout(timer);\n          if (msg.error) reject(new Error(msg.error.message));\n          else resolve(msg.result);\n        });\n        channel.postMessage({ id, kind: 'request', method, params });\n      });\n    } finally {\n      channel.close();\n    }\n  }, { method, params, timeoutMs });\n}\n\n/**\n * Install a sibling BroadcastChannel that records every `proc.stdout`\n * chunk the page-side bus server emits. Bounded so a runaway build log\n * can't exhaust page memory.\n */\nasync function installStdoutCollector(page) {\n  await page.evaluate(() => {\n    if (globalThis.__rwbUiStdoutChannel) return;\n    globalThis.__rwbUiStdout = '';\n    const ch = new BroadcastChannel('rust-web-box/webvm-bus');\n    ch.addEventListener('message', (ev) => {\n      const m = ev.data;\n      if (m && m.kind === 'event' && m.topic === 'proc.stdout' && m.payload && typeof m.payload.chunk === 'string') {\n        globalThis.__rwbUiStdout += m.payload.chunk;\n        if (globalThis.__rwbUiStdout.length > 2_000_000) {\n          globalThis.__rwbUiStdout = globalThis.__rwbUiStdout.slice(-1_500_000);\n        }\n      }\n    });\n    globalThis.__rwbUiStdoutChannel = ch;\n  });\n}\n\nasync function readStdout(page) {\n  return await page.evaluate(() => globalThis.__rwbUiStdout || '');\n}\n\n/**\n * Extract the first `println!(\"…\")` literal from Rust source and decode the\n * handful of escapes a hello-world greeting can contain. Mirrors\n * `firstSourceGreeting` in the harness so Step 1 asserts on whatever the\n * staged disk actually seeds — robust across the version-skew window where a\n * PR build may stage a previously published disk image. Returns null when no\n * println is found.\n */\nfunction extractGreeting(source) {\n  const m = String(source).match(/println!\\(\\s*\"((?:[^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*)\"/);\n  if (!m) return null;\n  return m[1]\n    .replace(/\\\\n/g, '\\n')\n    .replace(/\\\\t/g, '\\t')\n    .replace(/\\\\\"/g, '\"')\n    .replace(/\\\\\\\\/g, '\\\\');\n}\n\n// Strip CSI/SGR escapes (cargo colourises \"Compiling\"/\"Finished\") so plain\n// substring assertions are robust. The server already filters the\n// workspace-sync and cargo-bench OSC frames before they reach proc.stdout.\nfunction stripAnsi(s) {\n  return String(s)\n    .replace(/\\x1b\\][^\\x07\\x1b]*(?:\\x07|\\x1b\\\\)/g, '')\n    .replace(/\\x1b[\\[\\]][0-9;?]*[A-Za-z]/g, '')\n    .replace(/\\x1b[=>]/g, '');\n}\n\n/**\n * Poll the captured terminal output until the slice after `sinceIndex`\n * contains every needle in `contains`. Throws a diagnostic error (with the\n * tail of what we did see) on timeout so a stuck build or a corrupted edit\n * surfaces its cause, not just \"timed out\".\n */\nasync function waitForTerminalOutput(page, { contains, sinceIndex = 0, timeoutMs, label, intervalMs = 2000 }) {\n  const needles = Array.isArray(contains) ? contains : [contains];\n  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;\n  let lastDelta = '';\n  for (;;) {\n    const full = await readStdout(page);\n    const delta = stripAnsi(full.slice(sinceIndex));\n    lastDelta = delta;\n    if (needles.every((n) => delta.includes(n))) return { full, deltaStart: sinceIndex };\n    if (Date.now() >= deadline) {\n      const tail = lastDelta.slice(-3000);\n      throw new Error(\n        `[ui-e2e] timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms waiting for ${label} ` +\n        `(needed all of ${JSON.stringify(needles)}).\\n` +\n        `--- terminal output tail (ANSI-stripped) ---\\n${tail}`,\n      );\n    }\n    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, intervalMs));\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Focus the integrated terminal's xterm surface so subsequent\n * page.keyboard input is delivered as real keystrokes\n * (handleInput -> proc.write). Tries a few selectors across VS Code\n * versions.\n */\nasync function focusTerminal(page) {\n  const selectors = [\n    '.terminal-wrapper.active .xterm-screen',\n    '.terminal-outer-container .xterm-screen',\n    '.xterm-screen',\n    '.terminal .xterm',\n    '.xterm',\n  ];\n  for (const sel of selectors) {\n    const el = await page.$(sel);\n    if (el) {\n      await el.click();\n      return sel;\n    }\n  }\n  throw new Error('[ui-e2e] could not find the integrated terminal (.xterm) to focus');\n}\n\n/**\n * Focus the Monaco editor showing main.rs. Clicks the main.rs tab first\n * (it auto-opens active, but a stray welcome tab could steal focus), then\n * clicks the visible text region so the caret lands in the document.\n */\nasync function focusMainEditor(page) {\n  const tab = await page.$('.tab[aria-label*=\"main.rs\"]');\n  if (tab) {\n    try { await tab.click(); } catch { /* tab may already be active */ }\n  }\n  const selectors = [\n    '.editor-group-container.active .monaco-editor .view-lines',\n    '.editor-instance .monaco-editor .view-lines',\n    '.monaco-editor .view-lines',\n  ];\n  for (const sel of selectors) {\n    const el = await page.$(sel);\n    if (el) {\n      await el.click();\n      return sel;\n    }\n  }\n  throw new Error('[ui-e2e] could not find the main.rs Monaco editor to focus');\n}\n\n/** Type a command into the focused terminal and submit it with Enter. */\nasync function runInTerminal(page, command) {\n  await page.keyboard.type(command, { delay: 8 });\n  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');\n}\n\n/**\n * Handshake: prove the terminal is wired end-to-end (xterm -> proc.write\n * -> bash -> proc.stdout -> our collector) before we depend on it. Retries because\n * the pty's open() (which calls proc.spawn) fires shortly after the\n * extension reveals the terminal, and keystrokes typed before that are\n * dropped.\n */\nasync function The `webvm:` `FileSystemProvider` reads/writes\n38\tthis store directly via the bus, so VS Code's Explorer populates **the\n39\tmoment the workbench mounts** — no waiting for the 30+ second CheerpX\n40\tboot.\n41\t\n42\tWhen the VM finishes booting, `webvm-server.js` mirrors the JS-side\n43\tworkspace into the guest's `/workspace/` directory by writing a temporary\n44\tshell script to CheerpX's `DataDevice` mount and executing it\n45\tnon-interactively from `/data`. The visible login shell starts after that\n46\tprime step with `/workspace` as its working directory. Subsequent saves\n47\tfrom the editor write to both stores: JS-side immediately, guest-side via\n48\tthe same quiet `/data` script runner.\n49\t\n50\tThis is why the page can show a working Explorer + editor + open file\n51\tthe moment VS Code mounts — the alternative (gating the workspace on\n52\tCheerpX mounting an ext2 over the network) gives the user an empty\n53\tfolder for half a minute.\n54\t\n55\tThe page **looks identical to vscode.dev**. There is no custom UI: the\n56\tworkbench fills the viewport, the only chrome we add is a hidden\n57\tbottom-right toast that surfaces boot errors. The Rust toolchain comes\n58\tfrom a Linux VM running inside the page (CheerpX), surfaced as a VS\n59\tCode terminal labelled `WebVM bash`.\n60\t\n61\tVS Code Web runs each extension inside a dedicated Web Worker (the\n62\textension host). That worker has no DOM and no `SharedArrayBuffer`\n63\taccess to CheerpX, so the page (workbench document) holds CheerpX and\n64\teverything that needs raw browser APIs. The two halves talk over a\n65\tsame-origin `BroadcastChannel`:\n66\t\n67\t```\n68\textension worker  ──────────────────────  page\n69\t  webvm-host                                glue/webvm-server.js\n70\t   FileSystemProvider                        bus methods (fs.*, proc.*, vm.*)\n71\t   Pseudoterminal                            CheerpX (Linux + IDB overlay)\n72\t   Cargo tasks                               network-shim (cargo proxy)\n73\t```\n74\t\n75\tWhen the workbench mounts and the `webvm-host` extension activates, it\n76\tauto-opens a terminal pane that displays:\n77\t\n78\t```\n79\trust-web-box — in-browser Rust sandbox\n80\tPowered by CheerpX (leaningtech/webvm) and VS Code Web.\n81\t\n82\t[rust-web-box] Booting Linux VM… …………\n83\t[rust-web-box] Linux VM ready ✓\n84\t[rust-web-box] disk: ./disk/rust-alpine.ext2\n85\t[rust-web-box] Workspace mirrored to /workspace — try `cargo run`.\n86\t\n87\troot@rust-web-box:/workspace#\n88\t```\n89\t\n90\tThe status updates inline (no separate boot screen) — the user is\n91\texactly where they would be with `vscode.dev` plus a working terminal.\n92\t\n93\t## Component status\n94\t\n95\t| # | Component                       | Status | Notes                                        |\n96\t|---|---------------------------------|--------|----------------------------------------------|\n97\t| 1 | Page-level network shim         | ✅     | 18 unit tests; routes static/api direct, index via proxy chain |\n98\t| 2 | Service worker COOP/COEP cache  | ✅     | Caches shell + glue, synthesises COOP/COEP/CORP |\n99\t| 3 | CheerpX 1.3.3 loader + boot     | ✅     | Vendored at build time (engine + tun helpers); CDN fallback at runtime. The\n115\tdisk-image build pipeline (`web/disk/Dockerfile.disk`) starts from\n116\t`i386/alpine:3.20` (CheerpX requires i386 because it JITs x86 to WASM)\n117\tand installs only `bash`, `ca-certificates`, `curl`, `git`, `gcc`,\n118\t`musl-dev`, `pkgconfig`, `openssl-dev`, `rust`, `cargo`, `vim`, and\n119\t`nano`, plus `tree` for quick workspace inspection. We pre-bake a\n120\tminimal Cargo project at `/workspace` and run `cargo build --release`\n121\tinside the image so the first `cargo run` only re-links the binary,\n122\twell under the issue's 30 s acceptance bar on a warm disk.\n123\t\n124\tThe committed manifest still keeps the public WebVM Debian disk as a\n125\tdevelopment fallback. Production Pages builds are stricter: the staging\n126\tstep must download the rolling release asset and generate same-origin\n127\tCheerpX GitHubDevice chunks, or the build fails. That prevents Pages\n128\tfrom silently deploying a sandbox without `cargo` or `tree`.\n129\t\n130\t### Why \"🟡\" for rust-analyzer\n131\t\n132\tThe official rust-analyzer project does not currently publish a\n133\tready-to-use VS Code Web extension WASM bundle. The Rust Playground's\n134\tanalyzer is a custom build wired into that page, not a reusable artifact.\n135\tThe extension here ships:\n136\t\n137\t- Rust language ID + bracket/auto-close config (works immediately).\n138\t- Lightweight diagnostics so the extension surfaces *something*.\n139\t- A loader that reads `rust-analyzer.wasm` from the extension URI when\n140\t  available.\n141\t\n142\tVendoring an actual WASM build is a follow-up; the path is documented\n143\tinline in `web/extensions/rust-analyzer-web/extension.js`.\n144\t\n145\t## Acceptance criteria → status\n146\t\n147\t| #   | Criterion                                                              | Status |\n148\t| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |\n149\t| 1   | Open the site without sign-in                                          | ✅ |\n150\t| 2   | Full VS Code Web shell, indistinguishable from `vscode.dev`            | ✅ AMD-loader bootstrap from `vscode-web` npm, no custom chrome |\n151\t| 3   | Built-in terminal opens working `bash` inside WebVM                    | ✅ auto-opens with loading status, surfaces VM-ready, drops to bash |\n152\t| 4   | First load <2 min on 50 Mbps                                           | 🟡 depends on disk image size; SW caches subsequent loads |\n153\t| 5   | Edit `src/main.rs`, run \"Cargo: Run\", see output in <30 s              | ✅ wired; runtime depends on warm cache (Alpine image pre-builds hello-world) |\n154\t| 6   | `rust-analyzer` provides completion/hover/diagnostics                  | 🟡 extension wired, full WASM payload follow-up |\n155\t| 7   | Pre-baked crate compiles with no network (airplane test)               | ✅ Alpine image carries `rust` + `cargo` + pre-built root Cargo project |\n156\t| 8   | Non-pre-baked crate installs via proxy chain in <60 s                  | 🟡 shim ready; cargo's network from inside CheerpX needs Tailscale (issue #1 deferred) |\n157\t| 9   | Reload preserves user files (IndexedDB overlay)                        | ✅ via `OverlayDevice(cloud, IDBDevice)` |\n158\t| 10  | Second-visit load <10 s (SW caching)                                   | ✅ SW caches all glue assets + bundles on first visit |\n159\t| 11  | CI builds VS Code Web + image + extensions, publishes Pages on `main`  | ✅ pages.yml (workbench + Pages + staged disk chunks) + disk-image.yml (release asset source) |\n160\t\n161\t## Network reality\n162\t\n163\tThe original issue assumed CheerpX exposes a `networkInterface.fetch`\n164\thook that the page could intercept — there is no such hook today. CheerpX\n165\t1.2.x networking is Tailscale-only because the browser cannot open raw\n166\tTCP. The two consequences:\n167\t\n168\t- The page-level `network-shim.js` is honest about what it does: it\n169\t  serves `fetch` calls *from the page* (e.g. JS code that drives crate\n170\t  fetching outside the VM, or future pre-fetchers), not arbitrary\n171\t  syscalls from inside CheerpX. The shim is small, well-tested, and\n172\t  drop-in once the underlying CheerpX integration accepts it.\n173\t- For **live cargo** to reach `crates.io` from inside the VM, the user\n174\t  has to either (a) opt in to Tailscale (a follow-up PR per issue #1's\n175\t  \"Out\" list) or (b) use the warm crate cache in a pre-baked disk image.\n176\t\n177\tThis PR ships path (b) ready and path (a) hooked up to CheerpX's\n178\t`networkInterface` configuration so the user can supply an authKey\n179\twithout further integration work.\n180\t\n181\t## Constraints carried forward from issue #1\n182\t\n183\t- **CheerpX license** — free for personal/educational/open-source use.\n184\t- **Large disk image hosting** — the full ext2 image is too large for\n185\t  normal Git tracking, so it lives as a Release asset. The browser does\n186\t  not read that asset directly; `pages.yml` downloads it in CI and\n187\t  deploys 128 KiB same-origin chunks for `CheerpX.GitHubDevice`.\n188\t- **Cold start** — 30 s – 2 min depending on connection. SW + IDB\n189\t  caching makes second visits fast.\n190\t- **RAM** — 1.5–2.5 GB for VS Code + WebVM + cargo. Mobile is mostly\n191\t  out of scope.\n192\t- **Public CORS proxies are best-effort** — sequential fallback +\n193\t  per-proxy error logging covers the common breakage modes.\n194\t\n195\t## How to verify locally\n196\t\n197\t```bash\n198\t# Unit tests (no deps):\n199\tnode --test web/tests/\n200\t\n201\t# Build the workbench (needs npm + network):\n202\tnode web/build/build-workbench.mjs\n203\t\n204\t# Local dev server with COOP/COEP headers:\n205\tnode web/build/dev-server.mjs 8080\n206\t# then open http://localhost:8080\n207\t\n208\t# Build the Alpine + Rust disk image (needs docker + sudo):\n209\t./web/disk/build.sh\n210\t# produces web/disk/rust-alpine.ext2\n211\t\n212\t# Stage the release asset into Pages-compatible GitHubDevice chunks:\n213\tnode web/build/stage-pages-disk.mjs\n214\t\n215\t# Existing Rust template still builds + tests:\n216\tcargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features && cargo test\n217\t```\n218\t\n219\tLive screenshot of the running app (boot screen showing CheerpX VM ready\n220\tinside the VS Code terminal):\n221\t\n222\t![rust-web-box: VS Code Web with WebVM bash terminal](./screenshots/boot-vm-ready.png)\n223\t"
