[2026-06-13T19:03:49.221Z] [INFO]     "originalFile": "Closes #41\n\n## What this PR does\n\nIt answers the issue on the review's terms — *\"redo the analysis from measurement; check the WebVM code; if we lack tracing, add it so we know the exact bottleneck; speed up the **actual** build with no workarounds; use only real `cargo run`.\"* So it **measures** the bottleneck, adds **in-VM tracing** so the bottleneck can be confirmed in the browser on real `cargo run`, ships a `cargo check` fast-feedback path, and writes up a measurement-driven case study.\n\nIt also reports an honest negative result: the linker swap that *looked* like the fix was disproven **by the project's own in-VM test** and reverted. That is the issue's \"double-check our solution is not fake, and we actually use the VM\" requirement paying off directly.\n\n## The measured root cause\n\nReproducible docker rig on the exact i386 Alpine toolchain the disk ships (`experiments/issue-41/`):\n\n1. **Native wall-clock is emulation-invariant noise.** Every profile config rebuilds the one-line edit in **0.14–0.27 s**. Native CPU work cannot explain the 6 minutes — something the *emulation layer* multiplies does. This rules out the whole \"do less codegen\" family.\n2. **The cost is filesystem syscalls over the IndexedDB overlay.** That rebuild issues **14,736 filesystem syscalls**. Natively they're free page-cache hits; under CheerpX each crosses the WASM/JS boundary into `OverlayDevice(cloud, IDBDevice)`. **The bottleneck is I/O, not CPU.**\n3. **Natively, the linker is the dominant syscall source** (`link_binary` ≈ 68 % of compile time; GNU `ld` walks the libc archive with thousands of `_llseek`/`readv` calls).\n\n## The headline finding: `lld` looked like the fix, but regressed the real VM — reverted\n\nPoint 3 made the linker the obvious lever: swapping GNU `ld` → `lld` cuts the rebuild's filesystem syscalls **14,736 → 2,157 (−85 %)** natively. Every native metric called it a win. **It was not** — the in-VM e2e proved the opposite, so it was reverted (commit `5fa7df3`).\n\nThe project's own `disk-image.yml` builds the image, boots it in headless Chromium via CheerpX, and (e2e subtest 2, \"Stage G\") edits `src/main.rs` and runs a **real** `cargo run` with a 180 s ceiling. The linker is the only variable across these three disk builds:\n\n| disk build | linker | CI run | subtest 2 `duration_ms` | result |\n|------------|--------|--------|-------------------------|--------|\n| `b861a2f` (pre-swap) | GNU `ld` | [27462524216](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-web-box/actions/runs/27462524216) | **58 459** (~58.5 s) | ✅ `ok 2` |\n| `7c66bc7` | `lld` | [27467098552](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-web-box/actions/runs/27467098552) | **221 307** (~221.3 s) | ❌ `not ok 2` — timed out |\n| `766eece` (lld + guard fix) | `lld` | [27468491003](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-web-box/actions/runs/27468491003) | **220 808** (~220.8 s) | ❌ `not ok 2` — timed out |\n| `5fa7df3` (lld reverted) | GNU `ld` | [27468794132](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-web-box/actions/runs/27468794132) | **64 443** (~64.4 s) | ✅ `ok 2` |\n\n**Why:** CheerpX x86→WASM-JITs guest code on first use, and `lld` is a far larger binary than GNU `ld`. Its cold-JIT cost more than erases the −85 % syscall saving — net **+160 s or worse** on the real rebuild (it hit the 180 s ceiling and was killed, twice). **Native syscall count was the wrong proxy for in-VM wall-clock.** Full write-up: [`experiments/issue-41/results/in-vm-ab.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-web-box/blob/issue-41-81a2dcc93013/experiments/issue-41/results/in-vm-ab.md).\n\n## The load-bearing speedup (already shipped in #17/#31, verified in-VM here)\n\nThe real `cargo run` rebuild is at **~58 s** in-VM thanks to the **lean dev profile** (`debug = 0`, `codegen-units = 1`, `incremental = false`) plus **warm pre-bakes** (debug *and* release `target/`), which let cargo's freshness check finish without re-allocating fragile CheerpX overlay inodes. This PR's e2e (the table above) is what verifies that number on the real VM and guards it against regression.\n\n## What this PR ships (net)\n\n- **In-VM tracing.** `vm.benchCargo` (`web/glue/cargo-bench.js`) runs the user's **real** `cargo run` / `cargo build` / `cargo check` across four phases (no-op run, one-line-edit run, edit build, edit check) plus an optional `rustc -Z time-passes` split, and ships per-phase wall-clock over the existing OSC-frame stdout channel. It only rewrites the existing `src/main.rs` inode and restores the baseline (never touches `target/`), reuses the real `cx.run` path, and is zero-overhead when off. `globalThis.__RWB_DEBUG_VM_TIMING` records per-`cx.run` wall-clock. *Measures* the build; does not replace it.\n- **A `cargo check` fast-feedback path** (NEW): the warm disk pre-bakes `cargo check` and the seeded `tasks.json` offers a `cargo check (fast)` task. `cargo check` skips codegen and linking (**1,029** vs 14,736 filesystem syscalls), so errors surface in seconds. It speeds up the edit→error loop — *not* `cargo run` itself.\n- **A measurement-driven case study** in `docs/case-studies/issue-41/`, backed by the `experiments/issue-41/` docker rig: the syscall/linker census, the front-end/codegen/link split, the anti-fake VM verification, the in-VM A/B above, and a ranked catalogue of every improvement option (incl. the rejected `lld`).\n\n## The bigger win, specified as the next step\n\n**S2 — move `target/` off the IndexedDB overlay** (in-memory mount): makes the remaining syscalls RAM-fast *and* removes the `a1` fresh-inode wedge that forced `incremental = false`/`codegen-units = 1`, which unblocks **S3 — re-enabling incremental compilation**. `vm.benchCargo` now makes the in-browser before/after measurable. Full ranked catalogue in the case study.\n\n## Files\n\n- **Tracing:** `web/glue/cargo-bench.js` (new) + `web/glue/webvm-server.js`; tests in `web/tests/cargo-bench.test.mjs` and `web/tests/webvm-server.test.mjs`.\n- **`cargo check` path + e2e guard:** `web/disk/Dockerfile.disk` (pre-bake + `tasks.json`), `.github/workflows/disk-image.yml` (smoke test + e2e), `web/tests/e2e/local-pages-e2e.test.mjs`.\n- **Evidence:** `experiments/issue-41/` (docker rig + `results/`, incl. `in-vm-ab.md`), `docs/case-studies/issue-41/README.md`.\n- **Note:** `web/disk/Dockerfile.disk` keeps **GNU `ld`** — the `lld` change was reverted in `5fa7df3`.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `node --test web/tests/*.test.mjs` → **272 pass / 0 fail**\n- `cargo fmt --all --check` → clean; `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` → clean; `cargo test --all-features` → **19 pass / 0 fail**; `cargo test --doc` → clean\n- **In-VM, on the real VM:** disk-build run [27468794132](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-web-box/actions/runs/27468794132) (`5fa7df3`) is green — e2e subtest 2 reaches and passes Stage G's edited `cargo run` at **~64 s** (`# tests 4 / # pass 4 / # fail 0`), well under the 180 s ceiling.\n- Reproduce the measurements: `cd experiments/issue-41 && docker build -f Dockerfile.measure -t rwb-issue41-measure . && docker run --rm -v \"$PWD/results:/out\" rwb-issue41-measure /measure-linker.sh`\n\n",

[2026-06-13T19:03:53.021Z] [INFO]     "originalFile": "Closes #41\n\n## What this PR does\n\nIt answers the issue on the review's terms — *\"redo the analysis from measurement; check the WebVM code; if we lack tracing, add it so we know the exact bottleneck; speed up the **actual** build with no workarounds; use only real `cargo run`.\"* So it **measures** the bottleneck, adds **in-VM tracing** so the bottleneck can be confirmed in the browser on real `cargo run`, ships a `cargo check` fast-feedback path, and writes up a measurement-driven case study.\n\nIt also reports an honest negative result: the linker swap that *looked* like the fix was disproven **by the project's own in-VM test** and reverted. That is the issue's \"double-check our solution is not fake, and we actually use the VM\" requirement paying off directly.\n\n## The measured root cause\n\nReproducible docker rig on the exact i386 Alpine toolchain the disk ships (`experiments/issue-41/`):\n\n1. **Native wall-clock is emulation-invariant noise.** Every profile config rebuilds the one-line edit in **0.14–0.27 s**. Native CPU work cannot explain the 6 minutes — something the *emulation layer* multiplies does. This rules out the whole \"do less codegen\" family.\n2. **The cost is filesystem syscalls over the IndexedDB overlay.** That rebuild issues **14,736 filesystem syscalls**. Natively they're free page-cache hits; under CheerpX each crosses the WASM/JS boundary into `OverlayDevice(cloud, IDBDevice)`. **The bottleneck is I/O, not CPU.**\n3. **Natively, the linker is the dominant syscall source** (`link_binary` ≈ 68 % of compile time; GNU `ld` walks the libc archive with thousands of `_llseek`/`readv` calls).\n\n## The headline finding: `lld` looked like the fix, but regressed the real VM — reverted\n\nPoint 3 made the linker the obvious lever: swapping GNU `ld` → `lld` cuts the rebuild's filesystem syscalls **14,736 → 2,157 (−85 %)** natively. Every native metric called it a win. **It was not** — the in-VM e2e proved the opposite, so it was reverted (commit `5fa7df3`).\n\nThe project's own `disk-image.yml` builds the image, boots it in headless Chromium via CheerpX, and (e2e subtest 2, \"Stage G\") edits `src/main.rs` and runs a **real** `cargo run` with a 180 s ceiling. The linker is the only variable across these three disk builds:\n\n| disk build | linker | CI run | subtest 2 `duration_ms` | result |\n|------------|--------|--------|-------------------------|--------|\n| `b861a2f` (pre-swap) | GNU `ld` | [27462524216](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-web-box/actions/runs/27462524216) | **58 459** (~58.5 s) | ✅ `ok 2` |\n| `7c66bc7` | `lld` | [27467098552](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-web-box/actions/runs/27467098552) | **221 307** (~221.3 s) | ❌ `not ok 2` — timed out |\n| `766eece` (lld + guard fix) | `lld` | [27468491003](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-web-box/actions/runs/27468491003) | **220 808** (~220.8 s) | ❌ `not ok 2` — timed out |\n| `5fa7df3` (lld reverted) | GNU `ld` | [27468794132](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-web-box/actions/runs/27468794132) | **64 443** (~64.4 s) | ✅ `ok 2` |\n\n**Why:** CheerpX x86→WASM-JITs guest code on first use, and `lld` is a far larger binary than GNU `ld`. Its cold-JIT cost more than erases the −85 % syscall saving — net **+160 s or worse** on the real rebuild (it hit the 180 s ceiling and was killed, twice). **Native syscall count was the wrong proxy for in-VM wall-clock.** Full write-up: [`experiments/issue-41/results/in-vm-ab.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-web-box/blob/issue-41-81a2dcc93013/experiments/issue-41/results/in-vm-ab.md).\n\n## The load-bearing speedup (already shipped in #17/#31, verified in-VM here)\n\nThe real `cargo run` rebuild is at **~58 s** in-VM thanks to the **lean dev profile** (`debug = 0`, `codegen-units = 1`, `incremental = false`) plus **warm pre-bakes** (debug *and* release `target/`), which let cargo's freshness check finish without re-allocating fragile CheerpX overlay inodes. This PR's e2e (the table above) is what verifies that number on the real VM and guards it against regression.\n\n## What this PR ships (net)\n\n- **In-VM tracing.** `vm.benchCargo` (`web/glue/cargo-bench.js`) runs the user's **real** `cargo run` / `cargo build` / `cargo check` across four phases (no-op run, one-line-edit run, edit build, edit check) plus an optional `rustc -Z time-passes` split, and ships per-phase wall-clock over the existing OSC-frame stdout channel. It only rewrites the existing `src/main.rs` inode and restores the baseline (never touches `target/`), reuses the real `cx.run` path, and is zero-overhead when off. `globalThis.__RWB_DEBUG_VM_TIMING` records per-`cx.run` wall-clock. *Measures* the build; does not replace it.\n- **A `cargo check` fast-feedback path** (NEW): the warm disk pre-bakes `cargo check` and the seeded `tasks.json` offers a `cargo check (fast)` task. `cargo check` skips codegen and linking (**1,029** vs 14,736 filesystem syscalls), so errors surface in seconds. It speeds up the edit→error loop — *not* `cargo run` itself.\n- **A measurement-driven case study** in `docs/case-studies/issue-41/`, backed by the `experiments/issue-41/` docker rig: the syscall/linker census, the front-end/codegen/link split, the anti-fake VM verification, the in-VM A/B above, and a ranked catalogue of every improvement option (incl. the rejected `lld`).\n\n## The bigger win, specified as the next step\n\n**S2 — move `target/` off the IndexedDB overlay** (in-memory mount): makes the remaining syscalls RAM-fast *and* removes the `a1` fresh-inode wedge that forced `incremental = false`/`codegen-units = 1`, which unblocks **S3 — re-enabling incremental compilation**. `vm.benchCargo` now makes the in-browser before/after measurable. The durability-safe form of the RAM-cache idea is exactly catalogued **S2** — RAM-backed `target/` (ephemeral, safe to drop) with *source* kept on the durable overlay. The new in-VM storage probe confirms the live mount table on the real VM.\n- **F2 — js + rust + wasm + web workers, maximum multithreaded?** It's **already** js + wasm + web-workers + `SharedArrayBuffer`: CheerpX owns the SAB on the page thread, the VS Code extension host runs in a Web Worker, and COOP/COEP cross-origin isolation is synthesized by the service worker. But the guest VM is **single-core** (`CheerpX.Linux.create` has no SMP option; `nproc` = 1), so `cargo -j` / parallel codegen cannot fan out and the bottleneck is **serial fs-syscall IO**, not CPU. The right levers are **S2 + S4**, not more threads — the `jobs1`-vs-`jobs4` A/B that proves this is wired into the bench.\n- **F3 — benchmarks runnable on demand via CI.** Shipped `.github/workflows/perf-bench.yml` (`workflow_dispatch`-only): a **native** i386 job and an **in-VM** job that times the user's real `cargo run`/`build`/`check` in the live CheerpX VM (plus the storage+CPU probe). Nothing runs on a local machine.\n- **F4 — full UI-driven e2e on demand, verifying every step.** Shipped `web/tests/e2e/ui-driven-e2e.test.mjs` + `.github/workflows/ui-e2e.yml` (`workflow_dispatch`-only): `cargo run` in the **integrated terminal** → assert seed greeting; edit `main.rs` in the **Monaco editor** with a unique per-run marker (real Ctrl+S save) → `cargo run` again → assert the **new marker** *and* `Compiling`.
